review_notes:
I reviewed all of RealSmoothOperator.lean (lines 1–82): ext_value, Smooth.ofReal_part_re/im, laplacian_constant, complexL_ofReal and exists_real_smooth_poisson. I also read the definitions and lemmas they use: SmoothRealFunction and localExpression (AnalyticSupport.lean); laplacianValue, laplacianValue_local, laplacian and laplacian_localExpression (GlobalOperator.lean); HasNormalizedPoissonSolution and normalizedPoisson; RealSmooth.ofReal, source and ofReal_source (RealSobolev.lean); and complexL_re/im (ComplexKernel.lean).

Candidates I considered and rejected:
(1) Folding `hl` into `rw [hf, ← g.laplacianValue_local φ i hi] at hh` in exists_real_smooth_poisson. This would leave `g.laplacianValue φ x` in `hh`, while the goal mentions `(g.laplacian φ).value x`. `laplacian` is an ordinary def, so it is unclear whether linarith would treat the two as the same term. The explicitly typed `hl` also helps the reader. I did not flag it.
(2) Using laplacian_localExpression instead. It talks about local coordinates `z`, but this proof works with values at the point `x`, so it does not shorten the argument.
(3) Using `exact_mod_cast hφ` / `push_cast` in place of the short `rw [hφ, Complex.ofReal_zero]` or the `rw [← Complex.ofReal_add]; congr 1; linarith` ending. This would save few characters and make the cast handling less explicit, so it is a matter of taste.
(4) ext_value's `cases`/`rfl` proof and the pointwise Complex.ext proof of complexL_ofReal are already short and standard.

The pattern in laplacian_constant also appears in RealSobolev.complexL_real. That is outside the target file and is about reuse, not about simplifying a proof here. Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean to check whether any of the rejected alternatives would actually compile.
